title: Constitutional Amendment/Early Voting
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment that would guarantee North Carolina voters the right to early voting in primary and general elections. If approved by voters in November 2026, it would require a minimum of 14 days of early voting with specific operating hours and same-day voter registration at early voting sites.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this amendment expands voting access by guaranteeing early voting opportunities, reducing long lines on Election Day and allowing working people more flexibility to vote. They contend that same-day registration during early voting removes barriers for eligible voters who may have missed standard registration deadlines, and that standardized minimum hours and locations ensure consistent access across all counties.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue that constitutionalizing early voting limits the General Assembly's flexibility to adjust election administration based on changing circumstances or county resources. They might also raise concerns about the costs of maintaining 14+ days of early voting with mandated staffing and hours, particularly in rural counties with smaller populations, and question whether same-day registration creates sufficient time for election officials to verify voter eligibility.
